Question: It is desired to construct a right triangle in the coordinate plane so that its legs are parallel to the \(x\) and \(y\) axes and so that the medians to the midpoints of the legs lie on the lines \(y=3x+1\) and \(y=mx+2.\) The number of different constants \(m\) for which such a triangle exists is
Solution:
The axis-parallel legs make it useful to write the vertices as
\[
A=(p,q),\qquad B=(p+a,q),\qquad C=(p,q+b),
\]
with the right angle at \(A\). Here \(a\) and \(b\) are nonzero signed coordinate differences, so this includes every orientation of the triangle.

The midpoints of the legs \(AB\) and \(AC\) are
\[
M=(p+a/2,q),\qquad N=(p,q+b/2).
\]
Thus the medians to the legs are \(CM\) and \(BN\). Their slopes are
\[
\frac{-b}{a/2}=-\frac{2b}{a},
\qquad
\frac{b/2}{-a}=-\frac{b}{2a}.
\]
All denominators are nonzero because \(a\ne0\). Writing the second slope as \(s\), the two slopes are \(4s\) and \(s\). Therefore, if \(s=3\), then \(m=12\); if \(4s=3\), then \(m=3/4\). These are the only possibilities.

We must also check that the specified intercepts permit both values.

For \(m=12\), use
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(-1/3,0),\quad C=(0,2).
\]
Then \(M=(-1/6,0)\) and \(N=(0,1)\). Both \(C\) and \(M\) lie on \(y=12x+2\), while both \(B\) and \(N\) lie on \(y=3x+1\).

For \(m=3/4\), use
\[
A=(0,3),\quad B=(4/3,3),\quad C=(0,1).
\]
Then \(M=(2/3,3)\) and \(N=(0,2)\). Both \(C\) and \(M\) lie on \(y=3x+1\), while both \(B\) and \(N\) lie on \(y=(3/4)x+2\).

Both constructions have nonzero horizontal and vertical legs. Hence there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) different constants \(m\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
